svg.text: One neural-network layer IS a matrix multiply
Each neuron: multiply every input by its own weight,
add them up (+ bias), then a cheap nonlinearity (ReLU).
Each line is a dot product: a run of multiply-then-add.
This layer: 2 neurons × 3 inputs = 6 MACs per input vector.
Rule: at one input at a time, MACs per layer = number of weights.
3. Process a batch of M inputs at once
Matrix × matrix = GEMM. MACs = N × K × M.
Every weight is now reused M times. This reuse is what makes batching pay off.
4. A whole model = a chain of layers, each one a GEMM followed by cheap elementwise ops
95%+ of the arithmetic in any model is in the GEMMs. CNN convolutions and transformer attention/MLP blocks are all GEMMs underneath.
